title: Personnel Control and Utilisation Practices and Procedures

lessons.title: Planning and utilising people in the mill
lessons.html:
Planning and utilising people in the mill

This workplace module requires you to apply personnel control and utilisation practices as a supervisor in a real feed mill. Your mentor will assess how you plan, allocate, monitor and develop people over a sustained period.

Workforce planning for a shift

  1. Start from the production plan: lines running, products, changeovers, cleaning and maintenance windows.
  2. Determine positions to fill: intake, mixer, pellet line, bagging, forklift, dispatch, cleaning.
  3. Check attendance and leave. Arrange cover using the skills matrix, never placing untrained people on authorised tasks.
  4. Balance workload: avoid one operator running two critical lines while others are idle.
  5. Plan breaks so lines stay manned and fatigue is managed.

Working time

The Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997 regulates working hours, overtime, rest periods, night work and leave. Your company's conditions of employment and any collective agreements apply these. Plan overtime within those rules and the approved budget, record it accurately and get the required approvals. Long hours increase fatigue and error, which matters in a mill with moving machinery and critical batching tasks.

Utilisation measures

MeasureWhat it tells you
Tonnes per labour hourLabour productivity
Overtime hours as a share of normal hoursWhether staffing matches workload
Absenteeism rateAttendance trends; possible morale or health issues
Training hours and sign-offsDevelopment of skills and cover
Idle timePoor planning or breakdowns

Use these to discuss improvements with management, not to blame individuals.

Attendance control

  • Record attendance accurately using the clocking system or register.
  • Follow up absence promptly and consistently, according to the leave and absence policy.
  • Look for patterns, such as frequent Monday absence, and address them privately and fairly.

lessons.title: Procedures for conduct, development and wellbeing
lessons.html:
Procedures for conduct, development and wellbeing

Applying company procedures

Your evidence must show that you correctly applied your company's people procedures, which reflect the Labour Relations Act 66 of 1995 and the Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997:

  • Disciplinary procedure: investigate, give the employee the chance to respond, apply consistent and progressive sanctions, keep records, involve HR.
  • Grievance procedure: listen, record, try to resolve at your level within the set time, escalate if unresolved.
  • Performance management: set objectives, review regularly, coach, and document improvement plans.
  • Leave and absence: apply the policy and keep accurate records.

Induction and training

  1. Induct every new employee and contractor: site rules, safety, PPE, emergency procedures, hygiene, feed safety basics.
  2. Assign a buddy or mentor for the first weeks.
  3. Train on SOPs with a sign-off before independent work.
  4. Update the skills matrix and plan refresher training.

Health, safety and wellbeing

  • Ensure people use PPE and follow lockout and permit rules.
  • Watch for fatigue, intoxication or illness that make work unsafe; remove the person from the risk and follow procedure.
  • Support access to employee wellness programmes where the company offers them.
  • Treat everyone with respect; deal with harassment or discrimination complaints according to policy.

Communication

Hold daily briefings and regular team meetings. Share results, explain changes, and listen to ideas. Work with shop stewards and safety representatives constructively.

Evidence for your portfolio

  • Shift plans and allocation sheets you prepared.
  • Attendance and overtime records you managed.
  • Records of a grievance or disciplinary matter you handled, with confidential details removed.
  • Induction and training records.
  • Mentor observation reports.

Key points

  • Plan people from the production plan and the skills matrix.
  • Plan working time within the BCEA and company rules; manage fatigue.
  • Use utilisation measures to improve, not to blame.
  • Apply disciplinary and grievance procedures fairly and consistently.
  • Induct, train and sign off people before independent work.
  • Protect confidentiality in your evidence.
